Finding: EMULATE: shared-myth opener as permission frame
Detail: The Mako piece opens a list entry with the frame 'כולנו גדלנו על המיתוס' (4 words — label only) before delivering a correction. This move grants the reader permission to have been wrong: the writer is correcting a collective belief, not an individual mistake. The result is zero defensiveness in the reader. Bari can use this to introduce a counterintuitive score finding without alienating the shopper who bought the 'wrong' product for years.

Finding: EMULATE: 'וחבל' as a two-syllable verdict stamp
Detail: Single-word editorial lament ('וחבל') appended after a factual observation functions as a compact voice signature — it marks the author as an opinionated insider rather than a neutral lister. The technique is distinctly Hebrew-editorial; English has no single-word equivalent. For Bari copy, a short trailing lament after a product finding adds personality without inflating word count.

Finding: EMULATE: comparative advantage folded into the praise, not listed separately
Detail: Rather than: 'product X is good; it also beats Y on speed,' the article folds the comparison into the main claim — the superiority over alternatives IS the description of the product. This avoids the two-sentence structure that reads as a checklist and instead gives the description momentum. For Bari product rows: lead with the differentiator, not the category label, and embed the 'vs. the competition' in the same breath.

Finding: EMULATE: first-person-plural self-inclusion in a mild critique
Detail: The closing paragraph of the Mako article implicates the writer alongside the reader — 'אנחנו נוטים' (we tend to) — when observing a bad habit. The plural dissolves any lecture tone. Softened further with 'לפעמים' (sometimes), the critique never becomes preachy. For Bari, when a product insight criticises a common shopper habit (e.g., chasing shiny packaging), the 'we' frame keeps the voice companionable rather than superior.

Finding: EMULATE: biological mechanism as the hope-close
Detail: The Ynet fertility article ends not with a motivational call-to-action but with a concrete biological fact: the relevant cells regenerate on a defined cycle. This grounds optimism in mechanism rather than in encouragement, which reads as credible rather than hollow. For Bari, when a product verdict implies a consumer can improve their buying choices, closing on the physiological or process reason that change works feels authoritative and honest.
